1.title: KQL for the SOC
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen: K Q L for the sock. It covers the exam area three. Perform threat hunting. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Identify the appropriate table to use in a K Q L query. Identify threats by using Kusto Query Language. Create Advanced Hunting queries. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: three. Perform threat hunting (twenty to twenty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: The shape of a KQL query
1.text: The shape of a K Q L query. A Kusto Query Language query starts with a table, then passes rows through operators separated by the pipe character.

1.title: The shape of a KQL query, continued
1.text: The shape of a K Q L query. The figure shows this: A K Q L query is a pipeline: table, filter, shape, summarize.

1.title: The shape of a KQL query, continued
1.text: The shape of a K Q L query. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: The shape of a KQL query, continued
1.text: The shape of a K Q L query. Time column. Defender X D R tables: Timestamp. Sentinel (Log Analytics) tables: Time Generated. Time filter. Defender X D R tables: where Timestamp ago one day. Sentinel (Log Analytics) tables: where Time Generated ago one day. Exam tip: Put the time filter first, then the other filters, then project only the columns you need. Filtering early is the main performance rule.

1.title: Core operators
1.text: Core operators. where. Filter rows by a predicate. project, project-away, project-rename, project-reorder. Select, remove, rename or order columns. extend. Add a calculated column. summarize... by. Aggregate (count, dcount, make set, make list, arg max, min, max). count. Number of rows (shorthand for summarize count ). distinct. Unique values. take or limit. N arbitrary rows (good for testing). top N by. The top N rows by a column.

1.title: Core operators, continued
1.text: Core operators. sort by or order by. Sort. union. Combine tables. join. Combine rows of two tables on a key. let. Define a variable or a reusable query. parse, mv-expand, make-series, render. Parse text, expand arrays, build series, draw a chart.

1.title: Core operators, continued
1.text: Core operators. ago(one day). One day before now. bin(Timestamp, one hour). Round a time to a bucket (used with summarize). arg max(Timestamp, ). The latest row per group. make set(x). Distinct values as an array.

1.title: String operators
1.text: String operators. equals equals. Exact, case-sensitive. equals about. Exact, case-insensitive. has. Matches a whole term; fast (uses the term index). contains. Matches any substring; slower. has any, in. Match any of a list. startswith, endswith. Prefix or suffix. matches regex. Regular expression (slow); prefer parse. !has,!contains,!in. Negations. Case-sensitive forms (has cs, contains cs, equals equals ) are faster. Terms of three characters or fewer are not indexed. Exam tip: has beats contains for speed. equals about and inabout ignore case; equals equals and in do not.

1.title: Joins
1.text: Joins. The default join flavor is innerunique: it removes duplicate rows from the left side by the join key. inner. Rows with a match on both sides (all matches, no de-duplication). leftouter. All left rows, matches from the right when they exist. leftanti or leftantisemi. Left rows with no match on the right (a "not in"). leftsemi. Left rows that have a match. fullouter. All rows from both sides. Join tips: put the smaller table on the left; filter both sides by time; project only the needed columns before the join; use kind equals inner to avoid de-duplication.

1.title: Choosing the table
1.text: Choosing the table. Process creation on devices. Device Process Events. Files created or changed. Device File Events. Network connections from devices. Device Network Events. Registry changes. Device Registry Events. Logons on devices. Device Logon Events. Email delivery and blocking. Email Events; attachments Email Attachment Info; U R Ls Email Url Info; clicks Url Click Events. On-premises identity. Identity Logon Events, Identity Query Events, Identity Directory Events. Cloud app activity. Cloud App Events. Alerts and their evidence. Alert Info, Alert Evidence. Security Event. Windows security events. Signin Logs, Audit Logs. Entra sign-ins and directory changes. sys log, Common Security Log. Linux logs; C E F logs. Azure Activity. Azure subscription operations. Office Activity. Office three sixty-five activity. Security Alert, Security Incident. Alerts and incidents. Exam tip: Read the data source in the scenario, then pick the table: process equals Device Process Events, email equals Email Events, Windows logon equals Security Event, Entra sign-in equals Signin Logs.

1.title: Good habits
1.text: Good habits. Size a new query with count first. Use take to test. Filter early. Avoid unscoped search and union; use search in (Table A, Table B). Project only needed columns. Prefer parse over regex. Use Process Unique Id instead of P I D plus start time to identify a process.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. An analyst filters command lines for the word "invoke" and wants the fastest operator. Which should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: has, which matches a whole term with the index. The has operator uses the term index and is faster than contains.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A hunter wants to see every process that started on devices in the last day. Which table holds this data? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Device Process Events, with one row per process creation. Device Process Events records process creation.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which query returns the number of failed sign-ins per user from Signin Logs? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Signin Logs where Result Type! equals zero summarize count() by User Principal Name. summarize aggregates rows by a column; project, extend and take do not group.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A hunter needs the devices in table A that do not appear in table B. Which join kind fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: leftanti, which keeps left rows that have no match. leftanti returns the left rows without a match on the right.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An analyst wants delivered phishing emails by sender over the past week. Which table should be queried in advanced hunting? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Email Events, which records email delivery and blocking. Email Events holds email delivery data including threat types.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A new query on a very large table runs slowly. Which change helps the most? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Move the time filter to the beginning and project fewer columns. Filter early on time and other columns, and project only the needed columns.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which time column do Defender X D R tables use? Answer: Timestamp. Question two. Which time column do Sentinel tables use? Answer: Time Generated. Question three. What is the default join flavor? Answer: innerunique.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which operator rounds times into buckets? Answer: bin. Question five. Which table has Windows security events in Sentinel? Answer: Security Event. Question six. Which operator is case-insensitive equality? Answer: equals about.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Pipeline: table where project summarize. Time: Timestamp (Defender), Time Generated (Sentinel); ago(); bin(). Strings: has fast, contains slow, equals equals case-sensitive, equals about not. Join: default innerunique; leftanti for not in; small table on the left. Tables: Device Process Events, Email Events, Identity Logon Events, Security Event, Signin Logs. Speed: filter early, project early, has over contains, no search.
